svg.title: A-000 Site Plan
svg.text: S T R E E T
Masonry wall cut by section — 200 mm
Internal stud or block partition, 120 mm
Single leaf door, swing shown to opening side
Glazed opening — arched head where noted
Element above the cut plane (pergola, slab
1. The client's survey sketch recorded a 0.50 m step in the
north boundary and a 5.50 m offset between the two blocks'
north walls; the two cannot both be true. Resolved in
favour of a straight boundary at 18.00, with both blocks
running north to meet it. To be confirmed by measured
survey before any work starts on site.
2. The south wall of both blocks stands 1.50 m further into
the garden than the previous issue, giving each block a
14.50 m depth. The garden corridor is 5.00 m deep west of
the building and 3.50 m deep in front of it.
3. Upper floor balconies cantilever a further 1.20 m south of
that wall. Nothing projects over a boundary, but the
overhang is subject to the local projection rule; confirm
4. Only the west boundary is built against, so the west wall
is blind except where it faces the plot's own garden. The
north and east boundaries are open on the client's
confirmation and are windowed on every floor; the light
court shown in P3 has gone.
5. The ground floor sits 0.50 m above the garden, reached by
three risers at 167 mm at the entrance and at the patio
6. Structure is an RC frame on the grid shown, columns set
out on wall centrelines so none stands in a room; flat
slab where spans and layout make it the simpler solution.
Preliminary design issue — not for construction.
Do not scale; work to figured dimensions only.
P2 2026-09-24 east windows, taller floors, garden on A-100
P3 2026-09-29 four storeys, apartments, straight north boundary
P4 2026-09-29 north and east opened up, light court removed
